items.title: Nick Mondello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 19, 2022
items.q: It’s about Ryan Anthony, the late Ryan Anthony, the great Ryan Anthony and his cancer

ctx.x: If jazz is dead why are there still great schools like Berklee and North Texas State and Miami and whoever else I forgot to mention. Okay? These educational institutions aren’t just bringing in students under some kind of a false pretense. The other thing of course is the technological aspect of it plays a really, really, really big role. I’ll give you a good example. Before the Covid I went to see Randy Brecker, who is a dear friend, over at the resurrected My Father’s Place. And the feature artist there, it was…

got them hooked, and I’ll share one other thing, and I hope I’m not just going on and on — running on here. Okay? What I’d like to do is get students involved in things in addition to their school musical activities. Give you a good example: Trumpet players, would you like to be part of Taps Across America on Veteran’s Day or Memorial Day? You’ll be seen on YouTube, blah-blah-blah. Okay? We get them to play “Taps.” We did a thing with the World Band for a documentary that I’m involved in, an award-winning…
You’ve come a long way, baby.
